title: Graceful prefill admission and latency-tailoring for continuous batching
text:
Graceful prefill admission and latency-tailoring for continuous batching

description:
Implement a graded admission controller and latency-aware batch shaper for prefill + decode continuous batching. The goal is to reduce P99+ tail latency regressions under mixed workloads while preserving throughput for throughput-sensitive customers. Work spans runtime admission logic, a lightweight per-request priority token, integration with kernel selection heuristics (small vs wide kernels for attention), and a rollout-safe knob in the control plane.

acceptance_criteria:
P99 decode latency reduced by >=20% on the mixed-workload synthetic benchmark compared to current mainline under 95th percentile load pattern
New admission controller exposes two knobs: "grace_level" (0-3) and "burst_allowance" (tokens/sec) via API and console
No regression in aggregate throughput for Dedicated customers during canary (<=5% throughput drop on test harness)
Automated perf test added to CI that asserts median batch size and queue length targets for 3 representative request mixes
End-to-end canary run with gradual rollout policy and automatic rollback on latency SLO breach

tasks:
Design: finalize graded admission state machine and token accounting model (owner: Sana)
Runtime: implement admission tiers and fast-path for high-priority prefill requests (owner: Liam)
Kernel integration: surface admission hint to kernel selector so small-seq kernels are preferred when latency-critical admission is set (owner: Jordan)
Metrics: add histograms for prefill queue wait time, admission rejections, and per-tier batch size (owner: Ava)
Bench: extend perf harness with mixed RTT/length workloads and validate p99 improvements (owner: QA)
Console: surface new knobs and per-tenant default policy in Redwood Console (owner: Console UX)
Testing: unit tests for admission transitions, e2e perf test to CI, and load test script for canary (owner: Eng Reliability)
Docs: PRD update and runbook for operationalizing admissions and rollbacks (owner: PM)
Rollout: schedule canary on 3 Dedicated clusters with staggered percent traffic shifts and SLO gating (owner: Ops)
Postmortem: record any anomalies during canary in the incident tracker and iterate

comments:
2026-03-06 - Sana: Initial design doc uploaded to Confluence. Key decision: use a graded admission with four levels instead of binary admit/reject to reduce oscillation.
2026-03-08 - Liam: Prototype implemented in branch runtime/feature/graded-admission. Basic token accounting works but we observed higher than expected batch fragmentation in synthetic short-seq loads.
2026-03-09 - Jordan: Kernel selector updated to accept 'latency_hint' flag. Early microbench shows 8% faster single-token path when small-kernel selected.
2026-03-10 - Ava: Added metrics: prefill_queue_wait_ms and admission_reject_count. Hooked to dashboard: perf/continuous-batching/graded-admission.
2026-03-12 - PM Review (Nina): Requested explicit canary rollback criteria. Added P99 and P999 thresholds plus a maximum allowed throughput drop of 5%.
2026-03-13 - QA: End-to-end perf harness extended with client-mix: 60% short-chat, 30% assistant-long, 10% embeddings. Baseline runs captured.
2026-03-14 - Liam: Submitted PR #7423 for admission logic. Needs review from Jordan (kernel) and Ava (metrics). Noted trade-off: conservative grace_level reduces tail spikes but can increase average response time for long-seq workloads.
2026-03-14 - Ops: Scheduled canary start 2026-03-20 on cluster dedicated-us-west-2-a with 5% traffic, increment to 25% after 2 hours if metrics OK. Added automatic rollback webhook tied to latency-slo-prometheus-alerts.
Design note: We intentionally avoid strict per-tenant hard quotas in initial rollout to reduce customer-facing failures; prefer soft admission with token backlog ageing and dynamic decay.

implementation_notes:
Key trade-offs: aggressive admission reduces tail but fragments batches causing throughput loss for long requests. We will enable kernel-aware hints so the runtime prefers attention kernels optimized for short sequences when admitted at high priority. Prefill tokens are accounted separately from decode to avoid starvation. Admission decisions are cheap (lock-free counters) and evaluated on enqueue path to keep scheduling latency minimal.

rollout_plan:
Canary: 5% traffic -> 25% -> 100% over two days with automated SLO checks. If P99 latency or throughput thresholds breached, rollback to previous policy. Post-rollout, run 72-hour soak with increased telemetry sampling for P999 analysis.

risks_and_mitigation:
Risk: mis-tuned grace_level can throttle good traffic or not reduce tail. Mitigation: ship as opt-in per-tenant flag, collect telemetry, run A/B tests; provide quick rollback control plane toggle. Risk: kernel hint mismatch leads to suboptimal kernels; mitigation: metric gate and fallback to default kernel on degradation.

follow_up_items:
Investigate dynamic grace_level auto-tuning using live SLO signal
Evaluate integrating KV-cache locality into admission decision to favor cached contexts
Profile attention kernel shapes under admitted traffic to identify further micro-optimizations
